column1: # JuiceBar device catalog, read by both apps' cores (spec/PROVIDERS.md, spec/estimator.md).
# One row per thing a provider recognizes. Columns are tab-separated; "-" means none or unknown.

# match        receiver (USB product id of a receiver), dongle (USB product id of a device's own dongle), wpid (wireless product id a receiver reports for a paired device), usb (USB product id of the device itself on its cable); for game-controllers the vendor, since pads of two vendors share the provider: sony (product id under vendor 054C, USB or Bluetooth), microsoft (product id under vendor 045E, USB or Bluetooth)
# model        the name shown when the device does not report one
# kind         mouse, keyboard, headset, earbuds, gamepad, other

# battery      the battery source measured on the device: hidpp-0x1000, hidpp-0x1001 (voltage), hidpp-0x1004 (unified, percent), hidpp-0x1f20 (ADC, voltage); for game-controllers hid-ds5 (one DualSense input report sampled, percent in steps of ten), wgi (Windows.Gaming.Input battery report, else XInput levels)
# curve        the voltage-to-percent curve id in spec/curves.tsv, or "-" when the device gives a percent
# use_h        rated hours of use, lighting off (Logitech's figure); use_h_rgb the same with lighting on; charge_h rated hours to charge
# source       where the ratings and ids come from (docs/research/ file and section)

# short        the short name the panel, the tooltip and the notices show (the model without the family or the kind of product: G703, G915 X, DualSense); "-" for a receiver, which is never shown as a device
